description.narrative: At least eight districts in the eastern parts of Bangladesh were flooded due to heavy rainfall and upstream flooding in August 2024. Bangladesh Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) confirmed that five rivers in Moulvibazar, Habiganj, Feni, Comilla, and Chittagong were flowing above the danger level, leaving over three million people stranded. The Bangladesh Flood Response 2024-25 project aims to provide immediate relief and foster long-term recovery for flood-affected communities in Noakhali and Feni districts, as these two districts were marked among the worst affected areas by the government and UN-led flood coordination taskforce. This 1 million AUD project will support 37,909 beneficiaries from 8,816 flood affected households, especially ultra-poor & female headed households, religious and ethnic minorities, and people with disabilities etc. The project focus areas are food security, livelihood, protection, WASH, and NFI support.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: In 2024, Oxfam and local partners, with support from the Australian Government, provided humanitarian assistance to 4,520 individuals affected by severe flooding in Noakhali and Feni districts. The response prioritized vulnerable groups, including 3,626 women and girls and 1,115 persons with disabilities. ‍ The project delivered a comprehensive package of emergency relief and recovery support. Participants received multipurpose cash grants, food rations, Cash for Work, winter clothing, and winter vegetable seeds. These interventions addressed immediate needs while promoting long-term resilience.
